analysis:
Examined scripts/provider-release-publication.py base vs head. Head adds an optional cluster_runtime block (head 26-185) loaded only in prepare (head 247-262). It is size-bounded to 64 KiB, rejects duplicate keys, requires canonical JSON, and strictly validates schema, fields, digests (non-zero lowercase hex), sorted model IDs, grants, qualifications, envelopes and derived-ID length. validate() (head 215-222) re-checks the block and the registration-body size on stage/publish via checked_payload, so retained payload integrity is still bound to RELEASE_PAYLOAD_SHA256. registration_body (head 225-228) only changes serialization to compact JSON when the block is present. The bearer RELEASE_KEY (A-005) handling, the NoRedirect guard, the identity checks, the prod tag/source verification and the latest-alias logic are unchanged.

scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py is a new localhost-only test. It exercises a provider-cluster-runtime-models.py fetcher that was not supplied. The tests imply the fetcher refuses redirects, enforces size bounds, binds config.json to the manifest digest and fetches no weights. test-provider-release-pipeline.py was metadata only. Its range map shows release-provider.yml now allows continue-on-error on cluster runtime facts steps, which fail the job only when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true. No concrete regression was identified in the supplied source.

Integration questions, unverified and outside the supplied evidence:
(1) The comment at head 52-56 says the coordinator derives cluster approvals, grants and parity qualifications from the release registration. Those include the promotable flag and pair_serving_grant, which are self-reported by the signed app's `cluster runtime-facts` and the release lane. If the coordinator treats them as serving approval, then the release-publication key (A-005) would effectively confer cluster qualification. That would conflict with the independent-approval premise of A-017 and T-054 and may need a threat-model update (A-017/T-054/TB-011).
(2) The workflow change (release-provider.yml, provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh) and the models fetcher script need review. The fetcher reads coordinator and CDN catalog metadata over the network into release inputs (T-012/T-027 model-identity provenance).
(3) Dev payloads may also carry the block; confirm that dev-registered approvals cannot affect prod.
